games.title: Comprehensive Guide to Nutrient Digestion and Absorption: quick quiz
games.topic: Comprehensive Guide to Nutrient Digestion and Absorption
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which enzyme is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of disaccharides into monosaccharides in the small intestine lumen?
questions.explanation: Sucrase, along with other brush‑border enzymes such as lactase and maltase, cleaves disaccharides into monosaccharides for absorption.

questions.q: The majority of amino acid absorption occurs in which segment of the small intestine?
questions.explanation: The jejunum contains the highest density of transporters for amino acids, accounting for most absorption.

questions.q: Which transporter mediates sodium‑dependent glucose uptake in enterocytes?
questions.explanation: SGLT1 couples glucose transport with Na⁺ influx across the apical membrane of enterocytes.

questions.q: Chylomicron formation occurs in which cellular compartment?
questions.explanation: Chylomicrons are assembled in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and then packaged into secretory vesicles that travel to the Golgi for further processing.

questions.q: Which hormone stimulates gastric acid secretion by parietal cells?
questions.explanation: Gastrin binds to G‑protein coupled receptors on parietal cells, promoting H⁺ secretion.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the ileocecal valve?
options: Regulate flow of chyme into colon
questions.explanation: The valve controls flow and prevents reflux; it does not directly increase motility.

questions.q: Which transporter is responsible for the uptake of bile acids in the ileum?
questions.explanation: The apical sodium‑dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT) mediates ileal bile acid absorption.

questions.q: Which enzyme is secreted by pancreatic acinar cells and is essential for the digestion of proteins?
questions.explanation: Trypsinogen is activated to trypsin in the duodenum, initiating proteolysis.

questions.q: What is the primary site for the absorption of water and electrolytes in the gastrointestinal tract?
questions.explanation: The colon absorbs the majority of water and electrolytes from the remaining chyme.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the mechanism of vitamin B12 absorption?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 binds intrinsic factor and is absorbed in the terminal ileum via receptor‑mediated endocytosis.

games.title: Hematopathology: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 45‑year‑old woman presents with fatigue, pallor, and easy bruising. CBC shows hemoglobin 8.2 g/dL, platelets 45 × 10⁹/L, and a peripheral smear with anisocytosis and occasional schistocytes. Bone marrow aspirate reveals a hypercellular marrow with a 30% population of large blasts that are CD34+, CD117+, and TdT+. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: CD34+, CD117+, TdT+ blasts in a 45‑year‑old with pancytopenia point to B‑cell ALL.

questions.q: A 60‑year‑old man has a history of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and now presents with a sudden drop in hemoglobin from 12.5 to 8.0 g/dL and a platelet count of 30 × 10⁹/L. Peripheral smear shows numerous schistocytes and a few spherocytes. What is the next best step in management?
options: Order a coagulation panel for DIC
Obtain a CT scan of the abdomen
questions.explanation: The picture suggests microangiopathic hemolytic anemia; a coagulation panel for DIC is indicated.

questions.q: A 28‑year‑old woman presents with fever, night sweats, and a palpable left axillary lymph node. Excisional biopsy shows sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells that are CD20+, CD10+, BCL6+, and MUM1−. Ki‑67 is 90%. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Diffuse large B‑cell lymphoma, germinal center type
questions.explanation: CD10+, BCL6+, high Ki‑67, and CD20+ indicate DLBCL, germinal center type.

questions.q: A 70‑year‑old man with a history of hypertension presents with sudden onset of severe headache and vomiting. CT head shows a subarachnoid hemorrhage. Lumbar puncture reveals xanthochromia and a platelet count of 80 × 10⁹/L. Which of the following is the most likely underlying hematologic disorder?
questions.explanation: Acquired von Willebrand disease can cause spontaneous bleeding and thrombocytopenia.

questions.q: A 35‑year‑old man presents with painless splenomegaly and a peripheral smear showing numerous circulating nucleated red blood cells and a mild leukocytosis. Flow cytometry of the peripheral blood shows a population of CD34+, CD117+, and CD33+ cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Chronic myelogenous leukemia in blast phase
questions.explanation: CD34+, CD117+, CD33+ blasts in a 35‑year‑old with splenomegaly point to AML.

questions.q: A 55‑year‑old woman with a history of rheumatoid arthritis presents with anemia (Hb 9.5 g/dL) and thrombocytopenia (platelets 90 × 10⁹/L). Peripheral smear shows schistocytes and a few spherocytes. Which laboratory test would most help confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: A positive Coombs test would confirm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.

questions.q: A 42‑year‑old man presents with fever, night sweats, and weight loss. A lymph node biopsy shows a proliferation of small lymphocytes with a starry‑sky appearance and a high Ki‑67 index. Immunohistochemistry is positive for CD20, CD10, and BCL6. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Starry‑sky, high Ki‑67, CD10+, BCL6+ = Burkitt lymphoma.

questions.q: A 50‑year‑old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus presents with a sudden drop in hemoglobin and a platelet count of 25 × 10⁹/L. Peripheral smear shows schistocytes and a few spherocytes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Order a coagulation panel for DIC
questions.explanation: The presentation suggests TTP/DIC; a coagulation panel is the next step.

games.title: Cerebral Palsy: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 3‑year‑old boy presents with a stiff, spastic gait and a tendency to fall to the left when walking. He has a normal head circumference and no visual or hearing impairment. What is the most likely type of cerebral palsy?
questions.explanation: Spastic hemiplegia presents with unilateral spasticity and gait deviation.

questions.q: A 6‑month‑old girl has a high arched palate, microcephaly, and a floppiness that improves with age. She also has a mild intellectual disability. Which underlying cause is most likely?
questions.explanation: Zika infection is associated with microcephaly and spastic CP.

questions.q: A 4‑year‑old boy with spastic quadriplegia has a normal MRI but shows increased muscle tone in all four limbs and a positive Babinski sign. What is the next best step in management?
questions.explanation: Early physiotherapy is essential for all CP patients.

questions.q: A 2‑year‑old girl with spastic hemiplegia has a normal head circumference but shows a right‑sided spasticity and a left‑sided weakness. Which brain region is most likely damaged?
questions.explanation: Left hemisphere lesions cause right‑sided spasticity.

questions.q: A 5‑year‑old boy with spastic diplegia has a normal developmental milestone progression but shows a pronounced gait abnormality. Which imaging modality would best confirm the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: MRI is the gold standard for detecting periventricular leukomalacia.

questions.q: A 7‑year‑old girl with spastic quadriplegia has a normal intelligence quotient but exhibits severe speech delay. Which therapy is most likely to improve her speech?
questions.explanation: Speech‑language therapy targets speech delays in CP.

questions.q: A 3‑year‑old boy with spastic hemiplegia has a normal head circumference but shows a prominent left‑sided spasticity. Which of the following is the most common cause of his condition?
questions.explanation: Perinatal hypoxia is the most common cause of hemiplegic CP.

questions.q: A 4‑year‑old girl with spastic diplegia has a normal MRI but shows increased muscle tone in the lower limbs. Which medication is most appropriate to reduce spasticity?
questions.explanation: Tizanidine is a selective alpha‑2 agonist used for spasticity in CP.

games.title: Master pharmacology: drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which class of drug is theophylline classified as?
questions.explanation: Theophylline is a methylxanthine bronchodilator.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of amiodarone?
questions.explanation: Amiodarone blocks cardiac sodium channels, prolonging the action potential.

questions.q: Which drug is most commonly used as a first‑line treatment for acute asthma exacerbation?
questions.explanation: Albuterol, a short‑acting β2‑agonist, is first‑line for acute asthma.

questions.q: What is the characteristic side effect of clopidogrel that can lead to bleeding?
questions.explanation: Clopidogrel increases bleeding risk due to platelet inhibition.

questions.q: Which drug class is used to treat hypertension by blocking the renin‑angiotensin system?
questions.explanation: ACE inhibitors block the renin‑angiotensin system to lower BP.

questions.q: What is the main indication for the drug rivaroxaban?
questions.explanation: Rivaroxaban is an oral factor Xa inhibitor used for DVT prophylaxis.

questions.q: Which drug is known for causing a blue‑black discoloration of the skin?
questions.explanation: Chlorpromazine can cause a blue‑black skin discoloration.

questions.q: What is the mechanism of action of levothyroxine?
options: A. Inhibition of thyroid hormone synthesis
B. Replacement of deficient thyroid hormone
D. Blockade of peripheral conversion of T4 to T3
questions.explanation: Levothyroxine replaces missing thyroid hormone in hypothyroidism.
